MAJOR: AC-1 allowlist exempts `engineering/design/**` MD ("no content allowlist"), yet design MD is part of `review_scope` and gets indexed/rendered by `gen_docs_index`; if index rendering converts that MD to HTML, executable markup re-enters derived docs through the exemption — the chain-of-trust from `design_pack --fresh` output into browsable docs must be explicitly closed.

Grandfathering timeline is incoherent: cutoff is 2026-10-26 but expiry is 2026-11-01 (5-day window) while `grandfather_expiry` also mandates "warn 7 days before expiry" — the warning window starts before grandfathering even applies, and there is no lead-time before enforcement begins.

Grandfather list and the hard-coded expiry/`9dba2e3d` cutoff are not pinned to a named config source (`config/architect-review-baseline.json` or similar) with a hash; inline code constants make the back-compat rule change-by-commit and unreviewable.

`REVIEW_HEAD_STALE` is listed in `observability_codes` but no invariant defines staleness (review older than N days? older than latest push to review_scope paths?); an error code with no spec is implementer-interpreted.

"20MB/file cap" has no specified behavior on breach (fail closed vs skip) — silent skip would let oversized derived/excluded content evade validation, violating the fail-closed posture of `missing_created_fallback`.
MINOR: Timestamp normalization for the Generated header means a docs commit with only a newer timestamp passes the freshness gate; state explicitly that content-only comparison is the freshness definition (or that timestamp-only staleness is accepted).
"UTC ISO" parsing tolerance is unspecified (`fromisoformat` accepts offsets/naive forms); pin strictness (e.g., require `Z` or explicit offset, reject naive) in an invariant and test.

Rollback step 2 "regenerate docs" should be ordered after revert verification and include the assertion that post-revert gate run reproduces the pre-change docs hash; current order is implied, not verified.

`DESIGN_PACK_CONFIG` ownership in `design_pack.py` splits the stderr error-code contract across three scripts; a single shared error-code module (or a test importing all three) is needed so the codes stay a one-source contract.

Guardrail checklist items 2 (availability/SPOF) and 3/9 (authz/tenant) are answered only via "tooling only / no tenant data" strings; state explicitly "N/A — local developer-time CLI, no scheduler, no DB role, no RLS surface" to close CL-008/CL-003 cleanly.
NIT: `performance_bound` "O(changed files)" conflicts with a full-repo freshness check for committed docs; say "O(docs output) bounded, no network" or the bound will be misread during implementation.

`missing_created_fallback` "grandfathered" path inherits from the grandfather list rather than an explicit allowlist entry for that item id; naming it as an explicit per-item entry would remove the second implicit source.
`observability_codes` list and `failure_matrix` codes should be cross-referenced in one place (matrix as the source of truth) so the two cannot drift.
SUMMARY: Design v2/v3 correctly answers the Gate 1.5 BLOCKERs (CL-006 embedded findings/dispositions, pinned cutoff) and names validation owners, but three gaps remain: the design-MD content-allowlist exemption can bypass AC-1 through index rendering, the grandfather window (5 days) contradicts the 7-day warning contract, and the grandfather list/cutoff/expiry are not pinned to a reviewed config source.
`REVIEW_HEAD_STALE` and the oversize-file behavior are unspecified, leaving two fail-open risks in a gate whose stated posture is fail-closed.
Verdict: approve after MAJOR dispositions are ACTIONED in a design v3 with the timeline and config-pinning corrected; no blockers to a reversible, tooling-only rollout.
